questions.question: A spinner has 2 red sections and 2 blue sections. You spin it 20 times. What will MOST LIKELY happen?
options: About 10 red and 10 blue, close to even
Exactly 10 red and exactly 10 blue
All red, you got red the first two spins
All blue, because the last spin was red
questions.explain: With 2 red and 2 blue sections, both colours have an equal chance. Over 20 spins you will get close to 10 of each, but it will not be exact every time.

questions.question: You flip a fair coin 10 times. What is the MOST LIKELY outcome?
options: All heads, you got heads the first two times
About 5 heads and 5 tails, maybe 6 and 4
Exactly 5 heads and 5 tails, no more
All tails, you got heads three times in a row
questions.explain: A fair coin gives a 50-50 chance every flip. Over 10 flips you will get close to 5 and 5, but it could be 6 and 4, or 7 and 3.

questions.question: Leo flips a coin 3 times and gets heads each time. He says the next flip MUST be tails because it is due. What is the best thing to tell Leo?
options: Ten flips will give you exactly 5 heads
Three heads proves the coin only gives heads
The next flip is still a 50-50 chance
You must get tails now because heads came last
questions.explain: Each coin flip is its own new 50-50 chance. Getting heads three times does not make tails due on the next flip.

questions.question: Zara picks from a bag with 2 green balls and 2 purple balls. She does it 30 times and gets 16 green, 14 purple. Her brother says she should get purple 14 more times to make it even. What should Zara say?
options: I should have gotten exactly 15 and 15
You are right, purple is owed to me
30 picks prove I only ever get green
Each pick is still a new 50-50 chance
questions.explain: With 2 green and 2 purple, each pick is a fresh 50-50. You do not owe any colour — the next pick is still equal for both.

questions.question: A spinner has 2 red sections and 2 blue sections. You spin it 40 times. Your friend got 24 red and 16 blue. Is that a reasonable result?
options: Yes, 24 and 16 is close to even
No, you should get exactly 20 and 20
No, 40 spins prove red is always more
No, blue is due because red came up more
questions.explain: With 2 red and 2 blue, a 50-50 chance means 24 and 16 in 40 spins is a reasonable result. It does not have to be exactly 20 and 20.

questions.question: A bag has 5 red balls and 5 blue balls. You pick, replace, and do this 20 times. You get 12 red and 8 blue. Your friend says the next 4 picks MUST be blue to fix it. What is the best prediction for the next 4 picks?
options: All 4 blue, because they are owed to you
About 2 red and 2 blue, each is new
Exactly 2 red and 2 blue, no different
All 4 red, 12 proves red always wins
questions.explain: Each pick is a new 50-50 chance, so the next 4 picks should be about 2 red and 2 blue. Getting 12 red before does not make blue due.

questions.question: Tom spins a spinner with 3 green sections and 1 red section. He spins 30 times and gets 22 green and 8 red. He writes that he got red 2 times in a row, so red MUST come up the next 5 times. What went wrong in Tom's thinking?
options: He got red 2 times, so he proved it
He should have gotten exactly 23 green and 7 red
Getting red twice does not change the next spin
He is right, red is owed after so many greens
questions.explain: Getting red twice in a row does not change the chance of the next spin. The spinner does not remember what happened before.

questions.question: A spinner has 3 yellow sections and 1 green section. You spin it 50 times. Which colour will come up more often?
options: Green, yellow has had turns
Exactly 3 yellow to 1 green
Green, it came up twice now
Yellow, quite a lot more
questions.explain: Yellow covers 3 of the 4 sections, so over many spins yellow comes up far more often. Two spins are too few to tell, and the counts will not match the sections exactly.

questions.question: A spinner is half blue and half orange. You spin it 100 times. What is the best prediction?
options: About half blue, half orange
Mostly blue, it won twice
Exactly 50 blue, 50 orange
Mostly orange, blue had turns
questions.explain: Half and half means we expect close to 50 of each colour. Real results wobble a little above and below half, so they do not land on the exact number.

questions.question: A spinner has 2 pink sections and 6 grey sections. Ravi spins it 32 times. What should he expect?
options: Exactly 24 grey and 8 pink
Grey many more than pink
Pink more, it came up twice
Pink now, grey had a streak
questions.explain: Grey covers 6 of the 8 sections, so grey should come up much more often in 32 spins. The counts will land near that, not exactly on it.

questions.question: A spinner has 3 green and 3 white sections. Tia spins it 24 times. She gets 13 green and 11 white. Why is her result okay?
options: It must be 12 green, 12 white
Green is best, it won twice
Nearly half each is expected
White is due for 13 spins
questions.explain: With half green and half white, we expect each colour near 12, so 13 and 11 fits well. Many spins land close to even, not perfectly even.

questions.question: A bag has 6 blue marbles and 2 yellow marbles. Sam picks one, looks, and puts it back. He does this 40 times. What is the best prediction?
options: Blue exactly 30, yellow exactly 10
Yellow next 10, blue had a run
Yellow more, it came twice first
Blue about 30, yellow about 10
questions.explain: Blue is 6 of the 8 marbles, so about 30 of the 40 picks should be blue. Expect close to that number, because a short run of yellow does not change the bag.

questions.question: Rosa's class spun a spinner 40 times. They got green 31 and purple 9. The last two spins were purple. What is the best prediction for the next 40 spins?
options: Green again much more often
Purple more, it won the last 2
Exactly 31 green and 9 purple
Purple much more, it is due
questions.explain: Forty spins show green coming up much more, so green again is the best guess. Two purple spins in a row do not make purple due.

questions.question: Theo's spinner has 1 blue section and 3 red sections. He spins 3 times and gets blue each time. He says blue is the most likely colour. What should Theo do?
options: Trust the 3 spins he got
Spin many more and count
Spin now, red must be due
Spin till blue and red tie
questions.explain: Three spins is too few to tell anything. Many spins will show red winning, because red covers 3 of the 4 sections.

questions.question: Noah's team picks a cube to see who starts. The bag has 7 orange cubes and 1 grey cube, and the cube goes back each time. They pick 24 times. What is the best prediction?
options: Exactly 21 orange, 3 grey
Grey more, it came twice
Orange about 21, grey 3
Grey now, orange had a run
questions.explain: Orange is 7 of the 8 cubes, so orange should come about 21 times out of 24 picks. A run of orange does not make grey due next.

questions.question: Priya tosses a coin 20 times. She gets 9 heads and 11 tails. She says the coin must be broken. What is wrong with her thinking?
options: A fair coin has to give 10 and 10.
Tails is due, so toss ten more.
Heads is best because it won twice.
Nine and eleven is close to half.
questions.explain: In 20 tosses we expect about 10 of each, and 9 and 11 is very close to that. Real results almost never hit the exact number, so the coin looks fine.

questions.question: Jack and Lila share a bag of white and brown cubes. Jack picked 3 times, got brown twice, and says brown is more likely. Lila wants to pick 40 times and count. Whose plan gives the better answer?
options: Lila, more picks show more
Jack, white is due to stop
Jack, his two browns prove it
Neither, counts must be even
questions.explain: Many picks show which colour the bag really holds more of, so counting 40 picks is the better plan. Getting brown twice in 3 picks can happen by chance.

questions.question: At the school fair a bag holds 1 gold coin and 9 silver coins. Each of 50 kids picks one and puts it back. Emma picks first and gets the gold. What is the best prediction for the 50 picks?
options: Many get gold, like Emma did
About 5 of the 50 get gold
No more gold, Emma got it
Exactly 5 of the 50 get gold
questions.explain: Gold is 1 of the 10 coins, so about 5 of the 50 picks should be gold. One lucky pick does not make gold common, and the gold goes back in the bag.
